A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LiveEdit and contain complete main texts and supplementary material. Their methods, equations, tables, figures, and appendices can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original lifelong editing experiments, ablations, hyperparameter studies, and instance analyses, including the full benchmark results in supplementary Tables 5 and 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a difficult routing example and numerical per-expert resource costs.

M1.justification: The expert generator, visual-sentinel filtering, prompt-based soft routing, and training losses remain unchanged. The revised architecture diagram and added loss-balancing discussion explain the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate E-VQA, E-IC, and VLKEB using the same three VLLM backbones. The additional difficult VQA example does not establish a distinct task, domain, or test population.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain FT-L, FT-M, MEND, SERAC, TP, LTE, RECIPE, and LEMoE. MoVA is newly discussed as related work but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix 9 adds per-new-expert latency and memory as efficiency measures for LLaVA on an A800 GPU, without detailing the timing procedure. Existing dataset splits, edit counts, evaluation criteria, and training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix 8.2 and Figure 7 examine a difficult example intended to demonstrate complementary roles for hard and soft routing. Appendix 9 adds a brief resource-cost analysis. Existing ablations and hyperparameter studies are retained.

E5.justification: The uncertainty entries and Table 1 statement about t-tests at p < 0.05 are unchanged. Neither the new case nor the efficiency note introduces additional run counts, seed information, or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds a difficult example with new routing weights. Appendix 9 newly reports approximately 0.32 seconds and 160 KB per new LLaVA expert on an A800. Existing benchmark tables, ablation scores, and numerical plots in Figures 3–5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions and method equations remain substantively unchanged. Minor notation corrections do not alter the mathematics, and the new loss-balancing discussion supplies qualitative reasoning rather than a formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: LiveEdit, its generated experts and two-stage routing, a lifelong VLLM editing benchmark, and claims of superior editing performance.

C2.justification: Appendix 8.2 explains why choosing only the top visually matched expert can fail. Appendix 9 adds arguments about loss independence and alignment to justify unit weights, and states that the incremental time and memory per expert remain constant.

D1.justification: v1 states that code accompanies the supplementary material and will be released upon acceptance; v2 supplies an explicit public repository link. The new appendix also clarifies existing unit loss weights and documents per-expert resource costs.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MoVA reference and an explicit comparison covering task focus, intervention location, and coarse/fine routing. The broader related-work coverage and research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introductory method overview and LLM editing taxonomy, standardizes terminology, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The former Appendix 8 results become Section 8.1, alongside new Sections 8.2 and 9; the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer visual separation of expert generation and the two routing stages. Figures 1 and 6 receive label and layout refinements, and Figure 7 is added. Existing result-table structures and sensitivity plots are preserved.

improvement.justification: The clearer architecture diagram, explicit code-access information, and added loss and resource-cost discussions modestly improve explanation and practical documentation. The main empirical validation is unchanged. Figure 7 leaves the relationship between filtered experts and reported soft-routing weights unclear, limiting the value of that added evidence.
